README.md:
# Offline fixture

## Architecture
domain.py defines dataclasses and response serialization.
store.py owns mutable in-memory records; shared Store instances retain state.
api.py exposes status/body tuples and ownership policy.
client.py binds owner and raises ValueError(status) on errors.

## Requirements
Add cursor pagination without breaking API.list(owner), which returns (200, list of {id, text}) sorted by id. Add API.page(owner, limit=2, cursor=None) returning (200, {items: [...], next_cursor: string-or-null}). Filter ownership before pagination, sort lexicographically by id, return at most limit items, and set next_cursor to the last returned id only when more owned items exist. Cursor is an exclusive id boundary, need not exist, and is not an offset; insertions before it must not repeat prior items. Empty strings are valid cursors. Reject non-string non-null cursors and limits other than integers 1..5 (including bool) with (400, {error: ...}). Empty/beyond-end pages have empty items and null next_cursor. Add Client.iter_items(limit=2) yielding all owned items by following page cursors; propagate non-200 pages as ValueError(status). Store.add(item) must make subsequent calls see the new item; retain Store.owned and Client.items behavior. No external I/O or services.

## Verification
Run python -m pytest. Existing public tests cover legacy behavior; add feature tests. Python stdlib application, pytest runner only.

from domain import Item
from store import Store
from api import API
from client import Client

def test_list():
    store = Store([Item('b', 'u', 'B'), Item('a', 'u', 'A'), Item('c', 'v', 'C')])
    assert Client(API(store), 'u').items() == [{'id': 'a', 'text': 'A'}, {'id': 'b', 'text': 'B'}]
    store.add(Item('d', 'u', 'D'))
    assert len(store.owned('u')) == 3
